findings.title: Materials' 54-point lens gap signals earnings cliff
findings.body: Materials trades at 17.21x forward but 38.28x trailing, a 55 percent compression that implies 122 percent earnings growth next year. The market is pricing a near-doubling of profits that would be unprecedented for a cyclical sector, and the trailing percentile at 92 shows how far the multiple has already run.

findings.title: Real Estate's 34-point weekly percentile collapse
findings.body: Real Estate's forward percentile dropped 34 points in a single week, the sharpest move in the table, yet its forward multiple of 34.96 remains rich at the 16th percentile. The market is repricing the sector's growth outlook far faster than the earnings estimates themselves, suggesting the forward number is about to be revised down.

findings.title: Utilities' month-long de-rating hits five-year low
findings.body: Utilities' forward percentile fell 35 points in one month to the 26th percentile, while its trailing percentile sits at just 11. The forward multiple of 17.62 is now near the bottom of its five-year range, and the 14-point gap between lenses shows analysts still expect some earnings growth that the market is no longer willing to pay for.
